dedupe_keys.name: global food waste trade network before and after covid 19 2015 to 2024

description: This case study analyses how the international trade in food waste products changed around the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors, researchers at the University of Tehran and Shahid Beheshti University, built directed, weighted trade networks from World Bank export data for 2015 to 2024 and compared density, centrality and communities before and after the pandemic, publishing the work in an open-access journal article. Coverage is global at country level with annual flows. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: trade codes for food waste are broad, and export statistics miss informal and domestic flows. The study found that network density and connectivity stayed stable while average trade volume fell by 9 percent after the pandemic; the United States and European countries remained central, emerging economies such as India and Brazil formed new links, and community detection revealed a distinct emerging-economies trade bloc separate from traditional Western networks. Simulation uses: flow networks for modelling cross-border waste and by-product trade under disruption. Related records: the staple food trade network study (case_study-global-staple-food-trade-network-resilience-cascading-failure) applies similar network methods to staple crops, and Eurostat transboundary waste shipments (data-eurostat-env-wasship-transboundary-waste-shipments) records European waste flows.
